ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mismatch-Aware Vocabulary Conversion
PROPOSAL: Investigate theoretically guaranteed conversions of a next-token distribution to an equivalent distribution over an arbitrary subset of its vocabulary, without altering the text generation distribution. Use the Arora-Noe algorithm, known for yielding guaranteed approximations of NP-hard problems, to generate low-error conversions using limited oracle access to the original next-token distribution.
CONTROLS: Compare against existing token vocabulary misalignment mitigation methods, such as clipping and combining token distributions.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Verified conversions should be possible with bounded error, possibly learning more versatile vocabulary sampling methods in the process. The actual conversions may struggle with complex token relationships and fail on tasks that rely on nuanced vocabulary interactions. 

Also, for future reference, note the domains specified in the paper description include word problems/competition mathematics problem solving but don't fit with byte token approaches very well. We might want to selectively use the results on more token/byte agnostic tasks, like multi-subject multiple-choice question answering and machine translation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Task-Agnostic Vocabulary Reduction
PROPOSAL: Develop a task-agnostic approach to reducing the vocabulary of a pre-trained language model, using mutual information or similarity measures to identify and group low-information tokens. Evaluate this approach on multi-subject multiple-choice question answering and machine translation tasks, comparing against subsets based on token frequency and random sampling methods.
CONTROLS: Compare reduced-vocabulary models against their full-vocabulary counterparts on various metrics, including accuracy, perplexity, and inference speed. Also compare against the baseline in experiment 1 and a null model including the least frequent tokens at a rate proportional to baseline vocabulary frequency.
COST: 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Task-agnostic vocabulary reduction may improve the overall robustness of the language model by reducing our reliance on long tail vocabulary, but may also sacrifice performance on specific tasks requiring infrequent tokens.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Coordinated Vocabulary Expansion
PROPOSAL: Investigate the opposite scenario, where multiple language models with mismatched vocabularies try to learn to cooperate by expanding a coordinated vocabulary. Employ a meta-learning framework where the language models learn to learn from each other's outputs, thus dynamically adapting their vocabularies to better align. Evaluate this approach on realistic tasks like multi-subject multiple-choice question answering and machine translation, where domain adaptations could lead to knowledge transfer.
CONTROLS: Compare against ensembling results, as well as the performance on task-specific expansions of the original vocabulary. Repeat this experiment for language model pairs differing by the level of vocabulary mismatch.
COST: 800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This experiment may be brittle, since language models need to have some minimal common vocabulary to coordinate from, and will also likely require large datasets and computational resources. The effectiveness may greatly depend on the level of vocabulary mismatch to overcome and the specific architecture choices used.

CONTROLS: Compare with a random vocabulary subsetting baseline.
COST: 10 GPU-hours
